title: Schur polynomials twisted by roots of unity and reciprocal pairs: exactly three factors, and where they vanish
summary: Let $μ_t$ be the full set of $t$-th roots of unity. Adjoining $r$ free reciprocal pairs gives a two-parameter family of alphabets; we settle three parts of it. At $r=1$, for every $t\ge2$ and every $λ$ with at most $t+2$ parts, $s_λ(μ_t,z,z^{-1})$ is a signed product of exactly three factors over a fixed denominator, or zero, the arguments read off core and quotient. What it sees of $λ$ is a multiset of three integers and a sign, and exactly that: two partitions of any sizes share a nonzero value if and only if they agree on that datum.
